name: Śrī Jayatīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: born Dhoṇḍopant (Dhoṇḍo Pant Raghunātha), of a Deśapāṇḍe family; birthplace traditionally Maṅgalveḍhe near Pandharpur (one early source: Malkhed). In the Mādhva tradition (Uttarādi Maṭha), Indra with the āveśa of Śeṣa. The Ṭīkācārya commented on nearly all of Madhva's writings; chief works Nyāya-sudhā (on the Anu-vyākhyāna) and Tattva-prakāśikā (on the Brahma-sūtra-bhāṣya), among more than twenty. Samādhi at Malkhed (Mānyakheṭa), on the Kāgiṇī.

name: Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: Vilāsa-mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 195, 204); educated in Navadvīpa, then in Vārāṇasī under Madhusūdana Vācaspati. Chief work: the Ṣaṭ-sandarbha. He established the Rādhā-Dāmodara temple; the Deity, given by Rūpa Gosvāmī, is ordinarily dated 1542. Born c. 1513 (disputed); left this world traditionally in 1608 at Rādhā-Dāmodara (another account: 1598, with 85 years of life).

name: Kālidāsa
add: Nandgram Dham: of a kāyastha family, a distant uncle of Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī. He vowed for life to eat only the remnants (ucchiṣṭa) of Vaiṣṇavas of any caste, and in Purī received the Lord's own remnants (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 16). His neighbour was Jhaḍu Ṭhākura, a Vaiṣṇava of the bhūṁimālī (sweeper) caste.

name: Kālīya Kṛṣṇa Dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: also Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa; the ninth of Nityānanda's twelve gopālas. Ākāihāṭ is on the old road between Navadvīpa and Kāṭoyā; a festival is still kept there every year in Caitra. Nandgram Dham takes him as the Kṛṣṇadāsa who fell and was reclaimed on the Lord's South India tour (Madhya 10).

name: Kamalākara Pippalāi
add: Nandgram Dham: of a Rāḍhī brāhmaṇa family; the third of the twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 128; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.24). He took over the worship of Jagannātha, Baladeva and Subhadrā at Māheśa (Serampore); his title Adhikārī became the family surname.

name: Kāśīśvara Paṇḍita (Gaura-Govinda)
add: Nandgram Dham (which takes him as the same as Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī): disciple of Īśvara Purī, and so a godbrother of Mahāprabhu; a brahmacārī who served in Purī with Govinda, clearing the crowds before the Lord on the way to Jagannātha and distributing prasāda after kīrtana; son of Vāsudeva Bhaṭṭācārya of the Caudhurī family (not Sārvabhauma); as Bhṛṅgāra, a servant of Kṛṣṇa (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 137).

name: Śrī Kavi Karṇapūra
add: Nandgram Dham: born Paramānanda Sena (Paramānanda dāsa). His formal guru was Śrīnātha Cakravartī (Śrīnātha Paṇḍita), the family priest, of Advaita Ācārya's line, though he had received Kṛṣṇa's name from the Lord as a small child. Works: Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka, Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Ānanda-vṛndāvana-campū, Alaṅkāra-kaustubha and more. His last securely dated work is of 1576; no disappearance date survives.

name: Kholāvecā Śrīdhara
add: Nandgram Dham: also Śrīdhara Paṇḍita; he sold khola (banana bark used as cups) and the produce of his own banana orchard. His home is now Śrīdhara Aṅgana near Māyāpura, with a shrine built under Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī's direction, visited on the Navadvīpa parikramā.

name: Lord Kṛṣṇa
add: Nandgram Dham: also Govinda, Gopāla, Vāsudeva, Śyāmasundara, Hari, Madana-mohana, Jagadīśa, Puruṣottama, Vrajendra-nandana. Svayaṁ Bhagavān, the source of all avatāras, «kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam» (Bhāgavatam 1.3.28); the origin of the guru-paramparā, who has no guru and gave knowledge into the heart of Brahmā at the dawn of creation. See the Brahma-saṁhitā (ch. 5) and Jīva Gosvāmī's Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha.

name: Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: born c. 1496–1528 (sources disagree sharply); left this world c. 1615–1620 in Vṛndāvana (some traditions: 1616–1617). Names Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura as his direct disciple.

name: Kūrma Vipra
add: Nandgram Dham: also Kūrma Brāhmaṇa; his village at Kūrmakṣetra is identified with Śrīkūrmam, Srikakulam district (Andhra Pradesh). The Lord met him in Vaiśākha, c. 1510, and gave him the instruction «become a guru» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 7.121–135). His life after the tour is not recorded.

name: Śrī Lakṣmīpati
add: Nandgram Dham: a sannyāsī of the Madhva (Tattvavādī) order; his dates are not confirmed by any independent source. A photograph places his samādhi at Śrīraṅgam; no text confirms it.

name: Locana dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: born in 1523 (some sources 1520) in a vaidya family; parents Kamalākara dāsa and Sadānandī Devī; Kogrāma is near the Ajaya river. He finished the Caitanya-maṅgala in 1537; other works: Prārthanā, Durlabha-sāra, Dhāmālī, and Bengali verse translations of Rāmānanda Rāya's Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka and of the Rāsa-pañcādhyāya. His samādhi is in the 64 Samādhis area, Vṛndāvana.

name: Śrī Lokanātha Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: the descendants of his brother Pragalbha still lived in the family village. His close companion Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī was a relative and lifelong friend. His only known disciple was Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura. He found Rādhā-Vinoda at Kiśorī-kuṇḍa.

name: Lord Brahmā
add: Nandgram Dham: also Brahmājī, Svayambhū («self-born»), Prajāpati, Viriñci, Caturmukha, Aja, Hiraṇyagarbha. The secondary creator, a jīva in the highest post of this creation, born from the lotus of Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu's navel. He received from the Lord the catuḥ-ślokī of the Bhāgavatam (2.9.32–35) and taught Nārada, who taught Vyāsa; founder of the Brahma-sampradāya, root of the Brahma-Madhva-Gauḍīya line. He composed the Brahma-saṁhitā, whose fifth chapter Śrī Caitanya found in South India.
